burton_span.exact: O sad and odious name! a name so fell, / Is this of melancholy, brat of hell. / There born in hellish darkness doth it dwell. / The Furies brought it up, Megaera’s teat, / Alecto gave it bitter milk to eat. / And all conspir’d a bane to mortal men, / To bring this devil out of that black den. / Jupiter’s thunderbolt, nor storm at sea, / Nor whirlwind doth our hearts so much dismay. / What? am I bit by that fierce Cerberus? / Or stung by serpent so pestiferous? / Or put on shirt that’s dipped in Nessus’ blood? / My pain’s past cure; Physic can do no good.

1.4.1.1-f26.text: O triste nomen! o diis odibile / Melancholia lachrymosa, Cocyti filia, / Tu Tartari specubus opacis edita / Erinnys, utero quam Megaera suo tulit, / Et ab uberibus aluit, cuique parvulae / Amarulentum in os lac Alecto dedit, / Omnes abominabilem te daemones / Produxere in lucem, exitio mortalium. / Non Jupiter ferit tale telum fulminis, / Non ulla sic procella saevit aequoris, / Non impetuosi tanta vis est turbinis. / An asperos sustineo morsus Cerberi? / Num virus Echidnae membra mea depascitur? / Aut tunica sanie tincta Nessi sanguinis? / Illachrymabile & immedicabile malum hoc.

translations.note: Burton adapts Lucian's mock-tragic address to the Gout (in a Latin version), putting 'Melancholia' in place of the gout.

burton_span.exact: O sad and odious name! a name so fell, / Is this of melancholy, brat of hell. / There born in hellish darkness doth it dwell. / The Furies brought it up, Megaera’s teat, / Alecto gave it bitter milk to eat. / And all conspir’d a bane to mortal men, / To bring this devil out of that black den. / Jupiter’s thunderbolt, nor storm at sea, / Nor whirlwind doth our hearts so much dismay. / What? am I bit by that fierce Cerberus? / Or stung by serpent so pestiferous? / Or put on shirt that’s dipped in Nessus’ blood? / My pain’s past cure; Physic can do no good.

source.author: Lucian

translations.text: O mournful name! O hateful to the gods, / tearful Melancholy, daughter of Cocytus, / you, brought forth in the dark caverns of Tartarus, / a Fury, whom Megaera bore in her womb / and nursed at her breasts, and into whose mouth, when you were little, / Alecto poured bitter milk; / all the demons together brought you, abominable one, / forth into the light, for the ruin of mortals. / Jupiter hurls no such bolt of lightning, / no storm of the sea rages so, / no violent whirlwind has such force. / Do I endure the savage bites of Cerberus? / Is the venom of Echidna feeding on my limbs? / Or a tunic stained with the gore of Nessus' blood? / This evil is past weeping for and past all cure.
